# Vibhor Mathur

> Vibhor Mathur is a creative director and design leader based in Bengaluru, India. He leads Communication Design at Razorpay across Payments, RazorpayX and POS, and before that spent over six years at Grofers (now Blinkit), leaving as Associate Director, Marketing Design. His work spans brand films, integrated campaigns, interactive landing pages and AI-native production, including Trial of the Century, which won Generative AI at the Shorty Awards. Hire him for creative direction, brand film and campaign work, AI-led production, building an in-house design studio, or design mentoring.

## Key facts

- Currently: Communication Design Senior Manager, Razorpay
- Based: Bengaluru, India. Roots in Jaipur.
- Education: B.Tech, Computer Engineering. Government Engineering College Bikaner, 2010 to 2014.
- Languages: English, Hindi
- Email: onlyvibhor@gmail.com
- Behance: https://www.behance.net/onlyvibhor
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/onlyvibhor/
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/onlyvibhor/
- ADPList: https://adplist.org/mentors/vibhor-mathur

## What to hire for

- Creative direction for brand films and campaigns: Concept, art direction and craft for brand films, launch videos, keynote films and integrated campaigns, from brief to final edit.
- AI-native film and campaign production: Fully AI-made films and campaign systems that stay consistent at scale, such as 81 television films for 20 founders with no cameras, sets or lights.
- Interactive landing pages and games: Scroll-driven campaign sites and playable games that explain a product by letting people use it.
- In-house design team leadership: Hiring, developing and leading creative teams, and setting the visual system, process and tools they work in.
- Custom AI design tools for studios: In-house AI tools with real interfaces for cinematography, product imagery, image editing and founder-led campaigns.
- Design mentoring and AI-in-design workshops: One-to-one mentoring on ADPList, plus workshops, talks and panels on AI in design and design leadership.

## Frequently asked questions

### Who is Vibhor Mathur?
Vibhor Mathur is a creative director and design leader based in Bengaluru, India. He is Communication Design Senior Manager at Razorpay, where he leads Communication Design across Payments, RazorpayX and POS. From 2015 to 2021 he was at Grofers (now Blinkit), leaving as Associate Director, Marketing Design. He is a self-taught designer from Jaipur with a B.Tech in computer engineering.

### What can I hire Vibhor for?
Creative and art direction for brand films, launch videos and campaigns; AI-native film and campaign production; interactive landing pages and games; building and leading in-house design teams and visual systems; custom AI design tools for studios; and design mentoring or workshops on AI in design.

### What has he made with AI?
Trial of the Century, an AI film for RazorpayX Payroll, won Generative AI at the Shorty Awards. Break To Build turned one photograph of each of thirty founders into thirty ad films. Backing India's Start-Up Champions produced 81 television films, a newspaper front page and more than 200 social posts for 20 founders with no cameras, sets or lights. Back in the Ring is a fully in-house, fully AI-made cinematic trailer for Razorpay Netbanking.

### What awards has his work won?
Shorty Awards 2026: Winner, Generative AI; Gold Honor, Financial Services; Finalist, Community Engagement, for Trial of the Century. Kyoorius Creative Awards 2026: First List for Film Craft and for Use of Technology and AI. ET Brand Disruption Awards 2026: Gold, Most Disruptive Creative and Design Team, and Silver, Most Disruptive B2B Campaign.

### What results has his work delivered?
Backing India's Start-Up Champions reached 8.1 million unique viewers and lifted purchase intent by 133 percent. Trial of the Century earned more than 2.1 million impressions. The MoneySaver Export Account launch reached 29.1 million in media.

### What AI tools has his design team built?
The Razorpay design team built and uses a Cinematography Tool, a Product Image Generator, an Advanced Image Editor and a Founder Image Generator on live campaigns, all with proper interfaces rather than blank prompt boxes. The AI Toolkit page explains how each one works.

### Does Vibhor mentor designers or run workshops?
Yes. He is a design mentor on ADPList, where he has completed 33 one-to-one sessions of 60 minutes each. He also teaches workshops and joins talks and panels on AI in design and design leadership, including GrowthSchool, Designland and the IIIT-Delhi E-Summit.

### Where is he based, and how do I get in touch?
Vibhor is based in Bengaluru, India, with roots in Jaipur, and works in English and Hindi. The quickest way to reach him is email at onlyvibhor@gmail.com, or LinkedIn at linkedin.com/in/onlyvibhor.

Established a deck design language now used across more than ten product lines and business units.

## Case studies

### Trial of the Century
RazorpayX Payroll | 2025 | AI film · Campaign | Art Direction
An animal courtroom puts HR's most dreaded monthly question on trial.
A Panchatantra-style courtroom film that turned payslip confusion into a pop-culture moment for the HR community.
Reach the HR community, a relevant audience that is notoriously hard to engage.
RazorpayX Payroll needed awareness among HR professionals. They are the right audience, but a finance-heavy product is a tough sell to people who rarely engage with branded content.
A recent launch gave us a way in: an AI feature that lets employees talk directly to their payslips and ask salary questions. HRs showed genuine traction, which made us dig deeper into why.
The same questions, every month, and everyone had accepted it.
The moment salaries hit accounts, inboxes flood: Why did my salary change? What is this deduction? Not out of carelessness, but because payslips are dense with abbreviations, tax codes and compliance jargon that few people understand.
Over time the dependency became normal. HRs absorbed it, employees assumed it. That cultural resignation became our creative brief.
If the same questions come back every month, the system needs fixing, not the people.
We reframed repeated salary queries as a payroll design flaw and put the repetition on trial, in an animal courtroom inspired by the Panchatantra and an unmistakable piece of Hindi cinema, the sawaal pe sawaal courtroom scene from Damini.
- Porcumar Rao, a porcupine, takes every recurring query like a spoke in his back. - Chulbull Pandey, the aggressive bull, channels the courtroom cross-examination. - Hathiram Trankalp, a wise elephant, presides over the chaos. - The employees appear as a flock of chirping birds.
Within the story, RazorpayX Payroll introduces R.A.Y., an AI assistant that reads the payslip and explains any change instantly, in simple language, without HR stepping in.
- Explore: Character and mood explorations, iterated until the tone and personalities felt right.
- Lock the world: A digital map of the courtroom with every camera position fixed before a frame was generated: spatial logic instead of prompt randomness.
- Frame: Camera and framing prompts written with ChatGPT and Gemini, then executed through Nano Banana for consistent multi-angle shots, refined for continuity and texture.
- Animate: Performances generated and iterated until body language and facial expression felt natural.
- Voice: Professional voice actors chosen to embody each character, with lip-sync aligned to the recorded performance.
- Finish: Composited, edited and upscaled to 4K at 60fps.
We gave HRs a place to be heard, and a soundtrack.
The Wall of Laughter was an anonymous digital board where HR professionals shared the funniest salary questions they had ever received. Anonymity mattered: HR professionals are cautious about being seen online, so humour became a safe way in.
"Inbox Avalanche", a debut music single, turned the monthly flood into a hook and earned 4.5 lakh+ impressions and 50+ saves. B2B content, competing with entertainment.
The movement spread through HR communities across India, including The Shape of Work, People Matters, SHRM India, Being HR and HR Breakfast Club.
- 2.1M+ impressions
- 135K+ total engagements at an 8.64% rate
- 300K HR professionals reached, of a 650K online audience
- 300+ brand mentions
- 250+ reposts
- 13% uplift in D&O leads
The narrative shifted from "HR failure" to "systemic gap".
What began as a feature launch turned into a pop-culture moment inside the HR ecosystem, with startups across the space (Plum, Spring Verify, ClearTax, Smartstaff, Jify, Fi) engaging with a campaign that, for once, was about HR.

### Break To Build
Razorpay × JioHotstar | 2026 | AI film · IPL campaign | Art & Creative Direction
Thirty founders. Thirty ad films. Zero shoots.
A 100% AI experiment in making a TVC: founders photographed once, then broken, bent and built into cinematic films.
Back the founders building India, on the biggest stage in Indian marketing.
Razorpay's IPL 2026 push on JioHotstar. The ambition was to match the scale and spectacle of the tournament, while also stress-testing everything the design team had learned about AI workflows, tooling and design systems over the year.
What if breaking through was literal?
We took the campaign idea of breaking through and turned it into a visual statement: breaking, bending and defying the impossible.
Each one opens on what the founder was told.
Fine jewellery is for special occasions. An honest food brand will never work. Fresh food cannot scale. Pet care is not a need for India. Each film starts with the line a founder heard, and ends with "did it anyway".
Getting 30 busy founders in one frame? Almost impossible.
A shoot at this scale means complex schedules and a massive production budget. Breaking glass, breaking walls, breaking ceilings means high-risk shots, high production costs, and founders who are not actors.
AI made it possible. Thirty founders. One frame. Zero logistics.
- Shoot: Founders photographed once across carefully planned angles and poses.
- Style frames: We designed the visual language and built the worlds each founder would break through.
- Generate: AI transformed stills into cinematic environments, action and destruction.
- Craft: Shots were refined, composited and edited into finished films.
A stress test for everything the team had learned about AI.
Thirty ad films, a launch film, teasers, music and supporting content, produced AI-led from end to end: not AI-assisted, not AI-enhanced. It took collective conviction to say yes to something with no established playbook, on one of the biggest stages in Indian marketing.

### Backing India's Start-Up Champions
Razorpay × T20 World Cup | 2026 | Broadcast · Print · Social | Art Direction
India celebrates cricketers and founders equally. Only one gets a stadium. We built one for both.
81 television films, a newspaper front page and 200+ social posts for 20 founders, with no cameras, sets or lights.
Put founders on the screen cricket fans are already watching.
The T20 World Cup season is when the nation watches together. Razorpay set out to back its start-up champions where attention already was, treating founders the way the country treats cricketers: with a stadium, a jersey and a player card.
Designed to look like the broadcast, not interrupt it.
81 films. 20 match dates. Zero shoots. Each founder was lit three ways, warm daylight, floodlit blue and night drama, matched to every match slot.
Every film mirrored cricket player-card aesthetics: centre-composed, sportsman poses, stadium environment.
20 founders. One photo each. No shoots, no studios, no waiting.
A custom avatar tool, built on the Nano Banana API and Gemini AI Studio, took a single reference image and returned a full campaign visual library: sportsman poses, campaign costume, expressions tuned to each founder's personality. 4K output, one click.
Every founder walked into the campaign looking like they had always belonged on that stage.
Every founder. Every platform. One pipeline.
200+ extended social posts carried the campaign forward, including founders who did not appear in the TV spots. Drop in a founder photo and their business story and the pipeline returns a fully composed, campaign-ready post: title layouts per personality, costume, pose, lighting and background, all handled.
No individual design sessions. No back and forth. Just output.
The nation reads the paper. We put founders on the front page.
The same pipeline that built the TV assets produced full-page newspaper ads: same founder, same costume, same campaign language, in the hands of the same audience the morning after the match.
- 450K+ CTV impressions
- 8.1M unique viewers
- 928K LinkedIn impressions
- 133% purchase intent up

### Back in the Ring
Razorpay Netbanking | 2026 | Film · Landing page · Game | Creative Direction
A fallen champion, written off by one-tap payments, gets its redemption arc.
A boxing-film trailer, a parallax landing page and a playable game, built end to end in-house to relaunch Netbanking.
Bring Netbanking back into the conversation.
Netbanking had quietly powered online payments for decades. In the age of one-tap UPI and cards it felt like an old champion written off by everyone. The brief was to bring it back not as a legacy payment method, but as a trusted contender making its comeback.
- The film: Netbanking in the gym, drilling new features into knockout punches, training every round toward one goal: champion status, reclaimed.
- The arena: An interactive one-page landing page that breaks down the new tech powering the comeback, with parallax scrolling that pulls you deeper into the ring, every feature landing like a fresh combo.
- The game: Clear level after level; each opponent defeated unlocks a new feature, until the championship belt is back where it belongs.
A boxing film, not a product update.
Razorpay's Netbanking relaunch was told as a comeback story: a fallen champion, written off by one-tap payments, training its way back to the title. One idea ran across a trailer, a landing page and a playable game, so every touchpoint pointed to the same message: Netbanking is back, and here is what changed.
A fully in-house, fully AI-made cinematic trailer.
No camera crew. No actors. No sets. Just a design team, a handful of AI tools, and the conviction that Netbanking's comeback deserved to feel like a boxing film, not a product update.
That bet turned a brief for a 30-second UI video into a fully AI-generated cinematic trailer, premiering at GFF 26 in a category built almost entirely on dashboards and feature lists.
An AI-led design process.
The whole film was generated, organised and edited by the Razorpay design team across Higgsfield, Seedance and Pintor, with every generation collected in a shared gallery before it went to the edit.
Unmistakably Mumbai.
The desi boxing arena, Marine Drive, Aarey Colony, BKC big screens, chai tapri TVs: every location was chosen and art directed to feel unmistakably Mumbai. Not a generic city. This city. The All-India Digital Payments Championship gave Netbanking a world to be champion of.
Every costume tells the story.
Every character detail was locked: the worn grey hoodie with holed embroidery, the cobalt blue leather jacket, the boxing robe that fits versus the one that doesn't. Each costume carries the story, so the face never has to.
The clothing is the character.
Each character is identified by what is on their back: NETBANKING on the blue boxing robe, RAZORPAY on the cobalt leather jacket. By never showing a face, the film is never about a person. It is always about Netbanking, and the brand name is the hero in every frame.
One colour world for every act.
Warm amber for glory, desaturated olive for the fall, deep teal-orange for training, and punchy high contrast in brand blue for the comeback. The grade tells you where the story is before a single line is spoken.
Claude as a consistent creative director.
Claude was trained across the entire production workflow: shot composition, colour grade language, character continuity and art direction notes. It wrote the prompts for Pintor, Higgsfield and Runway, and the shots finished in After Effects and Premiere, so the hundredth shot matched the first.
From emotion to proof.
The landing page carried the film's world into the browser, then handed off from emotion to proof. Parallax scrolling pulls visitors deeper into the ring, each feature landing like a fresh combo, so they leave knowing what changed in Netbanking and how to switch it on.
Don't just watch the comeback. Play it.
A browser boxing game built into the campaign. Each opponent is an old Netbanking frustration, and each one defeated unlocks a new feature, until the championship belt is back where it belongs.
- Desktop Duke: The last man on desktop. Defeat him to unlock mobile-first.
- Typo Terror: Undefeated in wasted keystrokes. Defeat him to unlock QR-enabled payments.
- Click Titan: Heavyweight of unnecessary steps. Defeat him to unlock fewer clicks.
- Bounce Barry: King of the never-ending redirect. Defeat him to unlock no redirects.
- Partial Pete: Covers a handful of banks. Defeat him to unlock 100+ banks coverage.

### Magic Checkout Landing Page
Razorpay | 2026 | Landing page · Motion | Art Direction · Web Design
It's not just a checkout. It's engineered magic.
An immersive landing page that lets visitors experience what Magic Checkout does, instead of reading a list of features.
Don't explain checkout. Let people feel it.
The Razorpay Magic Checkout landing page turns a complex checkout technology into an immersive magical experience. Instead of simply explaining features, the page lets you experience what Magic Checkout does, making every step of checkout feel effortless and almost automatic.
One product story, four ways in.
The page is organised around four stories a merchant cares about: Boost Conversion, COD Control, Improve Purchase Intent and Build Loyalty. Each plays out on a floating island with a mock storefront, so the product screens sit inside a world rather than on a slide.
From the magic you see to the science behind it.
The experience shifts from an immersive magical world to a technical wireframe, revealing the data, logic and systems powering the seamless checkout experience.
Making every interaction feel alive.
A series of subtle micro-animations bring the interface and its features to life, adding moments of delight while making complex interactions feel intuitive and effortless.

### Agentic Commerce Engine Launch Video
Razorpay · GFF 26 | 2026 | AI film · Launch video | Art Direction
One founder's POV, one continuous world, one integration.
A 100% AI-made launch film for the Razorpay Agentic Commerce Stack, made for GFF 26.
Introduce one integration for agentic commerce.
Razorpay Agentic Commerce Stack: a launch film for GFF 2026 introducing one integration for agentic commerce across LLMs, concierge agents, WhatsApp and brand assistants.
Complexity gives way to the agentic era.
Told entirely through one founder's POV in a single continuous world, the film shifts from a grand marble hall to a glowing tech studio as complexity gives way to the agentic era, anchored throughout by a locked, high-contrast visual style built around her.
- Storyboard: Storyboarding and visual exploration to find the world and the character.
- Art direction: A carefully crafted art direction, locked early so every frame belongs to the same film.
- Key frames: Designing key frames for every environment and every human character.
- Generate and direct: Generating and directing the footage itself, frame by frame.
- Motion and stitch: Creating motion graphics and stitching everything into one cohesive narrative.
Every frame intentionally designed and refined.
The film was built under an incredibly tight timeline. The entire film was created using AI, from every environment and human character to the footage itself, and every frame was treated with the same level of creative direction as a full-scale film production.
Launch films from the same channel.
Two more Razorpay films: the Agent Studio social film and the RazorpayX corporate credit card film with RBL Bank.

### International Payments Launch Video
Razorpay | 2023 | Motion graphics · Launch video | Design & Motion
Launch video for the import flow of Razorpay International Payments.
A 40 to 60 second motion graphics film that makes international e-commerce payments simple to follow.
Show how Razorpay lets international businesses accept payments from India.
A dive into the world of international e-commerce payments, focused on Razorpay's solution that lets international businesses accept payments from India and settle in their own currency.
Demystify global e-commerce transactions in under a minute.
The challenge was to demystify the technicalities of global e-commerce transactions. The solution was a vibrant 40 to 60 second animation that makes the intricacies of international payments both understandable and visually compelling.
Motion graphics and kinetic animation.
The film transforms complex financial processes into a visual narrative using motion graphics and kinetic animation, created with Adobe Illustrator and After Effects. It resonated with the audience, earning over 1000 organic views.

### Magic Conversations Videos
Razorpay Magic Checkout | 2023 | Testimonial films | Design team lead
Two merchants on how Magic Checkout changed their business.
Testimonial films with Isak Fragrances and VS Mani Filter Coffees, shot and edited by a team of young designers learning the craft.
Merchants in their own words.
A testimonial video project that brings to life the experiences, and the tangible benefits, that two Razorpay clients, Isak Fragrances and VS Mani Filter Coffees, have enjoyed since integrating Magic Checkout into their e-commerce platforms.
Embracing the digital stage.
The first film was a venture into remote video production. Conducted over Zoom, it was new terrain for the team, pushing them to adapt and innovate. The result is a narrative of how Magic Checkout revolutionised Isak's online sales, told with authenticity and a fresh perspective by budding designers.
Learning in the field.
The second film was a different challenge: an on-site shoot at the client's office. It was hands-on learning for the team, who navigated the nuances of location shooting with determination, and the film captures how Magic Checkout transformed the business, seen through the lens of designers learning with every shot and edit.
Merchants on camera.
A newer set of Razorpay merchant reviews: Luzo, BookMyForex, ixigo and Mokobara.

### Passport For Your Product
Razorpay International Payments | 2023 | AI campaign | Campaign lead
AI-generated launch campaign for Razorpay International Payments.
A launch campaign whose entire design identity was built with a new AI workflow, then taken to YouTube, LinkedIn and Meta.
Make borderless business feel effortless.
Razorpay's Passport For Your Product campaign was a cornerstone of the International Payments launch. Cracking the brief took a new approach: an AI workflow introduced to establish a distinctive campaign design identity, positioning Razorpay as a forerunner in fintech by showing effortless global business expansion.
- Imagery: Midjourney conjured the compelling images that formed the campaign's visual backbone.
- Enhancement: Photoshop generative fill extended the images to every required dimension without losing their charm.
- Animation: The stills were set in motion, turning them into a seamless, flowing narrative.
- Edit: The voiceover and visuals were brought together to create a cohesive story.
High relevance, interaction and reach.
The brand campaign beat expectations with high relevance and interaction rates, leading to 35% lower buy rates. It achieved a 50% view-through rate on LinkedIn and substantial engagement on Meta. Distribution across YouTube, LinkedIn and Meta Ads maximised reach, with 94 leads generated, signalling strong interest in Razorpay International Payments.
The process was content too.
The behind-the-scenes video detailing the process was also well received on LinkedIn: over 60,000 impressions, and comments that appreciated the modern approach of using AI tools to push the boundaries of digital marketing.

### MoneySaver Export Account
Razorpay International Payments | 2023 | AI launch video | Campaign lead
India's first PA/PG with an OPGSP compliant solution, launched with an AI-made film.
A launch video and digital media strategy for the MoneySaver Export Account, made entirely with AI design tools.
A high-stakes launch for Indian exporters.
A launch campaign for the MoneySaver Export Account, marking India's first PA/PG with an OPGSP compliant solution, exclusively for Indian exporters. The project covered an innovative video and a comprehensive digital media strategy, positioning the product as a pivotal solution for exporters.
A first in the industry, crafted entirely with AI-based design tools.
The video was made with Midjourney, Studio D-ID and ElevenLabs. The goal was to capture the essence of the product: a platform that lets exporters open a bank account in their choice of country in under 5 seconds and save up to 50% on international transfer charges. Motion graphics and kinetic animation carried those points.
Razorpay's biggest product launch on its own platforms.
Over 438K views on Razorpay's social channels made it the biggest product launch there. Media coverage, including an exclusive interview on MoneyControl, led to 32+ stories and a reach of 29.1 million. The launch blog saw an 89.62% engagement rate with around 3K views, and the campaign generated over 70 high-quality leads.
Showing the AI workflow in the open.
A behind-the-scenes video detailed the use of AI tools in the campaign's creation. On LinkedIn that post received 1.2K likes, 83 comments and 33 reposts, with 313,315 impressions, and comments from the industry highlighted AI as a game-changer in marketing and B2B payments.

### Razorpay Payments on WhatsApp
Razorpay | 2023 | AI campaign | Campaign lead
Melancholy: the silent stories of abandoned carts. Shop. Don't abandon.
A launch film where AI-generated imagery tells sad stories of abandoned carts, then turns them into stories of completion.
Launch Razorpay payments on WhatsApp.
The campaign for Razorpay's payment solution on WhatsApp, led from concept to completion: coordinating teams, managing the creative process and using AI technology to make a campaign that is both innovative and emotionally resonant.
Melancholy.
Brainstorms with the marketing and design teams produced three campaign concepts. The chosen one, "Melancholy", delved into the emotive narrative of abandoned shopping carts in the digital realm, each with a story echoing the silent plea, "Shop. Don't Abandon."
- Imagery: Midjourney created the visual cornerstone: unique, emotionally compelling images of the silent stories of abandoned carts.
- Animation: Static images were brought to life into a flowing, dynamic narrative.
- Voice: A professional voiceover artist added a solemn tone that turns optimistic and energetic as Razorpay introduces its solution.
- Edit: Visuals and voiceover were edited together, with the visual style blending Razorpay blue and WhatsApp green.
The highest engagement rates on Twitter and LinkedIn.
With PR efforts, the launch video amassed over 95K impressions across social channels, with the highest engagement rates on Twitter (10%) and LinkedIn (4.5%). The accompanying blog captivated 6K+ unique readers, and 2000+ businesses expressed interest in the product, including a substantial number of existing Razorpay merchants.

### Grofers Logo Guidelines
Grofers | 2021 | Identity system | Art Direction · Graphic Design
How the Grofers logo behaves: space, shades, placement and hierarchy.
Logo usage guidelines for Grofers, covering clear space, colourways, placement, typographic hierarchy and in-app creative templates.
Give every team one way to use the logo.
A guideline document for the Grofers brand so that the logo, and the creatives built around it, look consistent wherever they appear. Created in Adobe Illustrator.
